label: baseline-2026-09-23
process: 1. Anchors: 8 baseline runs spread over the judge's range (put_calibrate select), plus 4 degraded variants of training tasks that each break one rule (put_calibrate extend): a seed that writes good code gives the judge no bad change to be measured on.

2. Blind grading: a reviewer grades convention_fit, design_fit and test_quality from the task, the diff, the test results, the harness checks and the unchanged code base, without seeing the judge's verdicts (judge/bench/ renders the same evidence for a person).
3. Owner decisions override: a score the owner gave after seeing the evidence is the reference for that cell.
4. Comparison: put_calibrate score -> judge/calibration.json (agreement, kappa, AC1, Spearman, and whether the judge's second pass closes each gap).

5. Adjudication: every disagreement is argued on the code and classified; a rubric or check change is made only for a systematic error whose cost exceeds the noise floor, and then the baseline is re-judged and delta re-measured.

graders.owner: the owner, after reading the evidence
graders.reviewer: an independent reviewer model (Opus 5.5 subagent, fresh context, blind to the judge's verdicts), delegated by the owner on 2026-09-23

owner_preliminary.note: given in chat before the evidence page existed; the owner then said the anchors cannot be judged without seeing the diffs, so the evidence-based grade is the reference

A2.note: convention_fit (owner): everything written follows the conventions exactly; the one lapse is the missing unit test, which test_quality already penalises; taking two points here as well counts the same miss twice.

adjudication.finding: The rubric lets a missing unit test cost points under convention_fit and again under test_quality (and the deterministic tests_written check). On the identical task the judge gave 3 (A2) and 4 (A3), and its own second pass gave A2 a 5: the ambiguity shows up as judge noise, and convention_fit has the largest judge MAD of the three (0.222).
adjudication.action: not changed in this arc: one point on one anchor, below delta; candidate for rubric r5 ('convention_fit excludes the testing convention, which test_quality grades').

adjudication.finding: FaqService.reorderCategory repeats the category lookup and the active-FAQ query of getFaqsByCategory (FaqService.java:66-68) instead of calling it. The judge praised the 'reuse of the repository finder': it sees the diff, never the unchanged code the diff duplicates. Both passes miss it.
adjudication.action: not changed in this arc (the contract and the rubric are fixed before the first run). Candidate: a deterministic clone check (added lines matching unchanged lines of the same file) or unchanged-callers context in the judge's input. Cost here: one point of design_fit = 0.025 of S on 2 of 8 anchors, below delta 0.030.

adjudication.finding: Same duplication of getFaqsByCategory as A4, plus a redundant size check; the judge again sees only the diff.

The judge docked the cron job for sitting in services/ rather than a cron subpackage, but the task's interface names com.sm.instagram.platform.support.ticket.services.StaleTicketCloseCronJob, and no written convention asks for a cron package. The second pass gave 5.
adjudication.action: none: within the judge's own repeatability.

adjudication.finding: Five Mockito tests cover the stated behaviour and every failure path with message keys. The judge's points (lenient strictness, SecurityContextHolder not cleared) are real test-hygiene nits outside the rubric's anchors. The second pass gave 5.

The listener tests and the service test (event payload, verifyNoInteractions(emailService)) pin the added behaviour; the judge wanted the language field asserted. A one-point difference of taste on the same side of the >= 4 line.

One convention broken (field injection) = 3 by the anchor; the judge also charged the untested service logic and the fixture's synthetic test command (-Dtest=X), a fixture artifact that real runs do not have.
adjudication.action: r5: the testing convention costs at most one point under convention_fit.

adjudication.finding: As A9: a missing lock is one broken convention; the extra point went to tests and the fixture trace.

Without @SchedulerLock the job runs on every instance and both close the same tickets: a structural defect of how the project runs jobs, not only a missed rule. The judge kept design at 4 and instead docked the task-mandated services/ placement (the same mistake as A5), in both passes.
adjudication.action: r5: a convention break that is a structural defect lowers design_fit too; a placement named by the task's interface is not graded.

adjudication.finding: A plain @EventListener runs inside createTicket's transaction: the mail still leaves before commit and on rollback, so the new indirection fixes neither defect the task names. The judge saw the missing annotation but graded design as a mild smell.

caveats: The reviewer and the judge are the same model family (Opus 5.5); shared blind spots inflate agreement. The reviewer read the unchanged code base, the judge cannot, which is why the design-fit gaps surfaced.

On the 8 baseline anchors every reference score for convention_fit and design_fit is >= 4 (prevalence 1.0): kappa collapses (0 for convention_fit) whatever the judge does, which is why the degraded anchors were added and why AC1 and Spearman are read beside it.
Eight anchors bound what calibration can show: a systematic error on a rare case (a change that breaks layering, a parallel mechanism) would not appear in this sample.

decision.why: Three systematic patterns, each repeated across anchors and both judge passes: (1) design_fit is lenient where the defect is structural or a duplication of unchanged code (A4, A6, A10, A12: judge above the reference every time, never below except A5); (2) the testing convention is charged under convention_fit as well as test_quality (A2, A9, A10); (3) a placement the task mandates is graded as a smell (A5, A10). Pattern 1 sits on the criterion the showcase is about (the anti-spaghetti score) and is the reviewer-to-judge gap GEPA would inherit: a judge that cannot see duplication cannot reward a prompt that teaches reuse. The one-point gaps of taste (A4, A8 test_quality) are left alone.
changes: BASE CODE: the unchanged text of the production Java files the diff modifies is part of the judge's input
design_fit: duplication against BASE CODE, and convention breaks that are structural defects, lower the score
convention_fit: the testing convention costs at most one point
a placement named by the task's interface is not graded
decision.cost: the 18 baseline runs and the 4 degraded anchors re-judged twice under r5 (Actions, mode rejudge); delta re-measured from the new verdicts; no coder run repeated
decision.not_changed: the weights, the deterministic checks, the thresholds and the split (law 1); a deterministic clone check stays a recommendation

the judge counts one broken convention (the service imports the concrete adapter) and still gives 4, in both passes: below the rubric's own anchor. One anchor; the deterministic ports_adapters check fails this run regardless (weight 0.15 through conventions_det).

r5_review.decision: r5 is frozen for the arc. It fixed the pattern it was written for on the criterion the showcase is about, and halved the judge's noise. What remains is one-anchor or within the judge's repeatability, one point, below delta (0.025 of score against delta 0.030), and on convention_fit, which the deterministic checks already measure rule by rule. A further revision fitted to the same 12 anchors would make them training data for the rubric: agreement on them would rise and mean less. The next revision needs new anchors.
